title: Recursive factorial
description:
Write a recursive function with a proper stack frame.

```
n: 10
10! = 3628800
fib(20) = 6765
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
ask:    db      "n: ", 0

        section .text
factorial:
        mov     eax, 1
        ret

_start:
        lea     rdi, [rel ask]
        call    print_str
        call    read_int
        mov     rdi, rax
        call    factorial
        mov     rdi, rax
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: `push rbx` / `mov rbx, rdi` / `lea rdi, [rdi - 1]` / `call factorial` / `imul rax, rbx` / `pop rbx` / `ret` (lesson 5.04).
`fib` needs to keep both `n` and the first result: push two registers, or one register and 8 bytes of padding so the next call is aligned.
requirements: Save the value you need after the call with `push`/`pop` or in a frame (`push rbp` / `mov rbp, rsp`).
`fib(n)` calls itself twice; keep the stack 16-byte aligned at each `call`.
stretch: Count how many calls `fib(20)` makes with a counter in `.bss`.
